To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and sequenced cDNA clones encoding A, B, and B2 chains of human laminin, and have demonstrated that the expression of laminin genes is not coordinately regulated in different human tissues and cultured cells.
human laminin is composed of three chains, designated A, B1 or alpha, and B2 or beta, and that the A, B1/B2 chains are encoded by three separate mRNAs.

the human A chain cDNA encodes 680 amino acids, the B1 and B chain cDNAs encode 1, 000 and 1, 200 amino acids, respectively, and the human A chain has a cell-binding Arg-Gly- Asp sequence that is absent from mouse laminin A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of cDNA clones encoding A, B2, and B1 chains of human laminin and with the expression of these chains in cultured human cells.
the molecular cloning and characterization of the human laminin A, 81, and B2 chains.
the cloning of cDNA encoding the A, B1 or B2 chains of human laminin and the expression of these chains in various cultured human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
laminin is a heterotrimeric molecule consisting of three polypeptide chains designated A, B1 (formerly called B) and B2 (formerly called B).

the three laminin chains are expressed in a coordinated manner in human skin and in cultured cells, with the exception of the A chain, which appears to be expressed at low levels in both tissues and cells.
human laminin is composed of three chains, A, B1 (formerly B) and B2 (formerly A), which are encoded by distinct genes and have distinct expression patterns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human laminin A, and B1, and possibly B2 chain mRNAs are expressed in a tissue-specific and cell-specific manner.
human laminin cDNAlibrary has been established and the A, B1,and B2 chain cDNA sequences have been determined.

human laminin A chain is encoded by a single copy gene, while B1 and B chain are encoded by multiple genes, with the B1 chain gene having a single copy and the B2 chain gene having two or more copies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laminin gene is expressed in a cell type specific fashion.
the laminin gene is not a single-copy gene in humans and that there is a significant difference in the expression of the A chain and B chain genes in cultured human cells and in human tissues.
the A chain mRNA is not a significant contributor to the human skin fibroblast.
